doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Learning on the job in Chicago bands
summary: DeJohnette says he was partly self-taught and learned improvising on the job in Chicago trios and bands; people wanted standards and blues.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yes. Well I wonder if you could talk about, you started out as a piano player playing classical music, and then you ended up, still at a young age, playing in bands. And was there a transition where you learned about how music is played without having it notated? And did you learn chords along the way? Was that an exploration of yours?
Yeah I did some of that, but a lot of improvising was involved you know, some of it self- taught, some of it was just you know I had trios and bands in Chicago and you know I
learned on the job you know. And I worked on things at home too you know. Same thing with drums.
When you went out to play gigs, I assume this was sort of in the late ‘50s, what kind of music made the people happy and that you needed to play?
People liked standards and they liked the blues and good heartfelt jazz you know.
